races.name: Country & Western Night 25th April Handicap

runners_data.name: Bang On The Bell

runners_data.comment: 12lb below his last winning mark; back to form at Nottingham a week ago; back on the AW

runners_data.name: Invitorio

runners_data.name: Anglesey Lad

runners_data.name: Poetic Jack

runners_data.comment: Promise in maiden/novice runs and excuses in two handicaps since; tongue-tie now added

runners_data.name: Desert Master
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong course record including a second place here in February
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who was second here in February; below his best in two starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Two of his three wins have been over C&D and he was second of eight here in a classified event in February; below his best in two starts since but he may be capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Hi Hoh Tonto
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse requiring pace collapse but has been well beaten in recent starts

runners_data.name: Noble Phoenix
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with known finishing issues and poor recent form trend

races.paceDynamic: Fortunate Star will take the field along with his confirmed front-running style, but with multiple prominent racers including Irish Dancer, Bang On The Bell, Anglesey Lad, Poetic Jack, Alfa Sea Breeze, and Desert Master all likely to track close, the pace will be honest rather than crawling. The two hold-up horses Invitorio and Hi Hoh Tonto will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their late kicks. With so many wanting to be handy in a 5f sprint, this race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and strike, rather than the pure pace-setter or the hold-up horses who may find insufficient pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent racers settle just behind Fortunate Star without excessive early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace becomes sustainable but honest, allowing the best prominent racer to time their challenge perfectly while Fortunate Star comes back to them in the final furlong. Hold-up horses find insufficient pace collapse and the leader tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Fortunate Star gets an easy lead with the prominent racers content to sit and wait too long
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow early, giving Fortunate Star enough in reserve to resist late challenges despite his front-running style being tactically exposed. The hold-up horses have no pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early pressure forces Fortunate Star to go too fast with multiple prominent racers scrapping for position
scenarios.body: The excessive early pace sets up a dramatic collapse in the final furlong, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past tiring leaders. Invitorio and Hi Hoh Tonto benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent racers refuse to commit early, creating a stop-start pace behind a crawling Fortunate Star
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair with no clear pace narrative, favouring the horse with the best finishing kick regardless of style. Desert Master's course experience could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Fortunate Star could get too easy a lead if the prominent racers are content to sit, making the front runner dangerous
Anglesey Lad returns from a 309-day break which could leave him short of race fitness despite the low weight
Multiple prominent racers including Irish Dancer, Bang On The Bell, and Poetic Jack could create early scrimmaging
Invitorio needs the pace to be genuine to set up his hold-up style but the tactical picture may not provide it
Desert Master's course form gives him an edge if the race becomes tactical given his twice-winning record here

races.name: Book The Bistro In Sherwood Restaurant Handicap

runners_data.name: Geordie Mackem

runners_data.comment: Down the field on his handicap debut over C&D 83 days ago; dropped 2lb; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in bumpers on his first two starts but he's yet to really threaten in this sphere; dropped 2lb since finishing down the field over C&D on his handicap debut 83 days ago and now has cheekpieces applied.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse

runners_data.comment: Won by 9l over C&D in October but well held on his next start; returns from 166 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Showed the benefit of a gelding operation when winning a C&D handicap by 9l in October but he was raised 8lb and was well held on his next start; needs to bounce back following a 166-day break.

runners_data.name: Shipshape
runners_data.note: Improving hold-up type who was second over this trip at Wolverhampton just 15 days ago, well-handicapped off 63

runners_data.spotlight: 0-7; shaped with encouragement here over 1m4f on his yard debut and backed up that impression when second of ten at Wolverhampton (1m6f, AW) 15 days ago; unexposed over this distance and he's a major contender.

runners_data.name: Moon Chime
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 204 days off with jockey taking over from previous rider, long absence is concerning

runners_data.name: Fashionelle
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare carrying just 122lbs with claiming apprentice, placed twice at this track in November
runners_data.comment: Placed here in November on two occasions; behind Shipshape at Wolverhampton last time
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 in Flat handicaps but she was placed here in November on two occasions (including C&D); behind Shipshape at Wolverhampton (1m6f) on his first start for 131 days but the returning cheekpieces should be a positive.

runners_data.name: Sycamore Gap
runners_data.note: Finally got off the mark at Newcastle in September, hold-up style suits if getting clear run from back
runners_data.comment: 1-17; didn't shape badly here over 1m4f on his return from 558 days off; back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 17th attempt when winning at Newcastle (1m4f, AW) in September 2024 on his final start for Rebecca Menzies; didn't shape badly here over 1m4f on his stable debut last time having been off for 558 days; may build on that over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Provision
runners_data.note: Struggled since switching yards and tackling hurdles, hold-up style needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Promise for Paul Midgley but has struggled in two starts for this stable; dropped 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in novice/maiden company when trained by Paul Midgley; struggled on his yard/hurdling debut in December and it was the same story in a handicap at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) three weeks ago; down 3lb.

races.paceDynamic: Mio Amico will lead from the gates with his prominent style, likely accompanied by Geordie Mackem who also likes to race handy. With only one true front-runner, Mio Amico can dictate a steady gallop over this 1m6f trip without early pressure. The large pack of hold-up horses (Betelgeuse, Shipshape, Fashionelle, Sycamore Gap, Provision) will be forced to sit behind the modest early pace before making their moves. This race shape strongly favours the early leaders and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably develop when six hold-up horses try to find racing room simultaneously in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mio Amico and Geordie Mackem establish a comfortable lead without interference from the field.
scenarios.body: The held-up brigade gets strung out behind the steady pace, and when they finally make their moves, the leaders have too much in hand. Mio Amico's recent Chelmsford victory at this trip proves his stamina, while Geordie Mackem gets the perfect scenario to finally deliver.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely steady and the hold-up horses get clear runs in the straight.
scenarios.body: Betelgeuse and Shipshape benefit from their proven stamina at this trip, with the former's 9-length C&D win in October showing his ability when right. The lack of early pace allows them to use their finishing kicks effectively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If Mio Amico goes too slow early and creates a bunched field turning for home.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a cavalry charge with multiple hold-up horses converging simultaneously, creating traffic problems. Sycamore Gap and Fashionelle, drawn better positioned, can take advantage of the chaos while others get squeezed for room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Geordie Mackem fails to support Mio Amico and the leader gets an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Mio Amico gets such an easy time in front that he builds an unassailable advantage before the field can organize a challenge. His recent form suggests he has the class edge when allowed to dominate proceedings completely.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems in the straight when six hold-up horses (Betelgeuse, Shipshape, Fashionelle, Moon Chime, Sycamore Gap, Provision) converge simultaneously
Monitor if Geordie Mackem can provide genuine support to Mio Amico early or leaves the leader isolated in front
Check if Betelgeuse shows any signs of rustiness after his 166-day absence, particularly in the first two furlongs
Watch for Shipshape's finishing kick given his recent Wolverhampton second and lightweight of Daniel Muscutt
Observe if the two claiming apprentices (Kyle McHugh on Mio Amico, Finlay Bassett on Fashionelle) can handle the tactical demands

races.name: Come Racing For Free 18th June Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Penny Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with recent winning form, will look to dominate from the start but stamina questioned over this trip

runners_data.name: Goldinthesea

runners_data.comment: Got off the mark over 1m at Dundalk on his second start; has since left Joseph O'Brien
runners_data.spotlight: Built on the encouragement of his debut when winning at Dundalk (1m, AW) in January, coming 3l clear; subsequently left Joseph O'Brien and now makes his stable debut; one to note in the betting.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Third pace angle who finished third last time, likely to be outgunned by the other front-runners but adds to tempo

runners_data.name: Niffler

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger

runners_data.name: Avispado

runners_data.comment: Showed little on his debut at Doncaster (6f, heavy); gelded since and steps up to 1m

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has shown some promise, tactical position could prove ideal if pace collapses but ability questions remain
runners_data.comment: Failed to build on his debut when fifth at Kempton in October; has been off since
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise when fifth of nine on his debut at Haydock (1m, good to soft) but he wasn't able to build on that when filling that same position behind a nice prospect at Kempton (1m, AW) 182 days ago; off since.

runners_data.name: Baron Wagstaff
runners_data.note: Sits handy in his races and ran behind Penny Time on debut, recent Bath effort disappointing but drops back in trip
runners_data.comment: Showed some ability on his debut but he was well beaten over 1m2f at Bath last time
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability behind Penny Time (subsequently disqualified) at Kempton (1m, AW) on his debut but he was well beaten at Bath (1m2f, good) ten days ago; drops back to 1m on this return to the AW; may be one for handicaps.

races.paceDynamic: Goldinthesea, Penny Time, and The Anthony Gover will ensure a strong early gallop in this novice stakes, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the lead from the start. The sustained pace over 1m on Southwell's tight track will test stamina reserves, particularly as these pace-setters have shown they don't easily relent. With multiple leaders creating genuine tempo, horses finishing from off the pace will get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and closers who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse in the final 2f.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain their aggressive early splits through halfway
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will take its toll on the leaders, allowing hold-up horses to sweep past tired pace-setters in the final furlong. Sassicaia and the debut runners with stamina pedigrees will benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters manages to steal a march turning for home
scenarios.body: Penny Time or Goldinthesea could kick clear of their pace rivals and hold off the closers, particularly if the tempo becomes more measured mid-race. Their recent winning form gives them the edge over The Anthony Gover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast and completely collapses
scenarios.body: Brighton View and Baron Wagstaff, sitting just off the leaders, could emerge from the wreckage to capitalize on their tactical positioning. They avoid both the pace scramble and the need for an extreme finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the experienced runners fail to handle the sustained pace demands
scenarios.body: One of the newcomers from powerful yards could exploit the tactical naivety on display, with Harmonics or Shadow Boxer having the breeding to stay this trip strongly. The Gosden and Crisford stables excel with patient debut tactics.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Penny Time and Goldinthesea to engage in a pace duel from the start, which could set up the perfect scenario for Sassicaia
Monitor the betting market for Harmonics and Shadow Boxer, as significant support would indicate stable confidence in these expensive debuts
Keep an eye on how aggressively The Anthony Gover breaks from the stalls, as three-way pace battles often result in complete collapse
Watch Brighton View's early positioning, as he needs to avoid getting caught up in the pace scramble while staying close enough to strike
Observe if any of the hold-up horses show early pace, which would compromise the strong gallop scenario that favours their profiles

runners_data.name: Embarked

races.paceDynamic: Embarked will take the field along at a sustainable gallop from the front, with no other natural leaders to pressure him. The real battle develops behind as Rusheen Boy, English Lady, Sixteen One, On Key and Aspire To Glory all want prominent positions, creating inevitable traffic problems and positioning battles from 3f out. This congestion allows the patient hold-up horses like Orbital Chime, Call Glory and Dancing With Drums to pick their way through late. The uncontested lead combined with prominent runners getting in each other's way strongly favours either the lone leader or those patient enough to wait in behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Embarked maintains his rhythm without pressure and the prominent pack gets tangled up
scenarios.body: The veteran gets first run on the field while the traffic-hit prominent runners can't organise their challenge in time. His 8-year-old experience counts as he holds off late challengers who leave their runs too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates gaps for patient trackers to exploit
scenarios.body: Orbital Chime or Call Glory threads through the carnage while Embarked begins to tire, timing their run perfectly as the leaders falter. The extra furlong suits their patient style over the speedier types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent pack avoids the traffic and gets a clear run at Embarked
scenarios.body: Rusheen Boy or English Lady finds racing room where others don't, using their natural speed to bridge to Embarked before he can consolidate. Their class tells in a straight fight with the struggling leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Embarked goes too fast early and the prominent pack falls apart completely
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery as tired leaders get swamped by everything, with any horse finding a clear passage capable of winning. Form and ratings become secondary to pure luck in running.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic chaos from 3f out as five prominent runners (Rusheen Boy, English Lady, Sixteen One, On Key, Aspire To Glory) fight for limited space behind Embarked
Monitor Embarked's early fractions - if he goes too keen without pressure he'll be vulnerable to late closers in the final furlong
English Lady and Rusheen Boy both return from long breaks but retain headgear, suggesting connections expect them ready to fire
Call Glory and Orbital Chime need the prominent pack to create a strong pace to set up their finishing kicks
Several runners stepping up in trip including Dancing With Drums who might appreciate the extra furlong after recent sprint wins

runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner with excellent recent form including 7f success, only 12 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Won at Lingfield on Good Friday, taking record this year to 3-5; progressive filly
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile filly who has gained wins over 5f, 6f and 7f on her way to producing a strike-rate of 3-5 this year; gained the latest success at Lingfield on Good Friday and may not have stopped improving yet.

runners_data.name: Beckon
runners_data.note: Prominent type dropping back from 1m to more suitable 7f trip, shaped with promise at this track previously
runners_data.comment: Drop back to 7f is worth exploring; may do better still and not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Ran below market expectations at Southwell (handicap debut) three months ago when bidding for a 1m double but shaped as if this drop back to 7f is worth exploring; may do better still and not written off.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner but exposed type still seeking first handicap success, 13 days since seasonal return
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced over C&D on reappearance but looks reasonably exposed
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced over C&D on seasonal debut; however, looks reasonably exposed and still needs to prove she can win a handicap, having gained her 2yo successes at maiden/selling level.

races.paceDynamic: Vencedora and Homestrait are confirmed early leaders who will contest the front from the gates, ensuring a genuinely run race from the start. The small field of seven creates limited cover, meaning the prominent runners like Cool Molly, Bee My Honey and Beckon will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal. With two dedicated front-runners ensuring honest fractions over 7f at Southwell, this race shape strongly favours horses with early speed and prominent tactics who can position handy and kick from the turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Running Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Vencedora and Homestrait engage in a prolonged speed duel from the gates
scenarios.body: The fierce early pace sets up the race perfectly for Cool Molly and Bee My Honey to track the leaders and pounce in the final furlong. Both have the tactical speed to sit prominent and the class to capitalise when the front pair weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners go at a more measured clip allowing tactical positioning
scenarios.body: Cool Molly's versatility and recent 7f Lingfield success positions her perfectly to control the race from a prominent berth. The small field limits cover options, making her tactical speed decisive against this field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Rogue Citation and Ribenska get their preferred scenario with a slowly run race that becomes a dash from the back. Their closing kicks become potent weapons in a bunched finish where positioning matters less.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of Vencedora or Homestrait gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to dictate comfortable fractions and kick clear approaching the final furlong. Vencedora's superior class edge makes her the more likely beneficiary of this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Vencedora and Homestrait could burn each other up with an unsustainable early pace battle given both are natural front runners
Cool Molly's quick turnaround of 12 days might tell late if the pace is strong early and she's forced to race prominently
Rogue Citation and Ribenska both return from long breaks exceeding 160 days which could impact their fitness first time back
The small seven-runner field creates limited tactical options with hold up horses Rogue Citation and Ribenska potentially caught too far back
Bee My Honey needs to bounce back from a poor last effort but has strong course form including a 7f success here

races.name: Summer Socials At Southwell Racecourse Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Barefoot Beach
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won at 25-1 last time but faces much stronger pace pressure here from two other confirmed leaders
runners_data.comment: 1-1 last term and positives to take from recent return; player on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Possibly significant she was declared to make her debut at Glorious Goodwood in July (non-runner) and scored at 25-1 when finally given the go ahead at Kempton (6f, Polytrack) in September; positives to take from last month's returning second over that C&D, despite the odds-on reversal, and she carries plenty of potential into this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer with C&D winning form who should benefit significantly from the expected strong early gallop
runners_data.comment: Kempton win and narrow Lingfield second off this mark; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner who last scored at Kempton (6f) off this mark in September; just edged out at Lingfield (7f, also Polytrack) on penultimate start and finishing last in a classy Newcastle handicap on Good Friday can be glossed over; not without a chance.

runners_data.name: Seven Fires
runners_data.note: Front-runner with highest TopSpeed figure (71) and proven at this C&D, but 33 days off could be a slight concern

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: Another confirmed leader returning after 158 days absence, which makes her stamina reserves questionable in a pace battle
runners_data.comment: Placed on first four starts; won fifth; respected on reappearance/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on her first four starts and put it all together when taking Wolverhampton novice (6f, Tapeta) in November; may have more to offer this term and she's respected on this reappearance and handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Mirage
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 173 days but has proven course form and the tactical profile to benefit from strong pace
runners_data.comment: Solid third on final start for George Scott; unexposed at this trip; seasonal/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Built on promising debut (6f, good) in August when landing Wolverhampton novice (Tapeta) three weeks later; back in that form when third in course handicap (also 5f) on final start for George Scott in October and sold for 17,000gns five days later; unexposed, particularly at this trip, and impossible to rule out on this stable/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with C&D winning experience but 184 days off represents a significant fitness question
runners_data.comment: Won her first two but the wheels came off after; handy mark on return; watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: 14-1 but she scored on her introduction over C&D in June and defied a penalty in Chelmsford novice (7f, Polytrack) the following month; reverse thrust firmly engaged after that and she didn't beat a rival on her last two starts of 2025; however, she's become attractively weighted and needs a market check ahead of this comeback.

runners_data.name: Addarella
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was beaten 10 lengths here just 5 days ago, making quick turnaround very difficult to recommend
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10l over her favourite C&D on Friday; not easy to suggest after that
runners_data.spotlight: Couldn't build on good 6f Wolverhampton record when beaten 10l over that C&D on Friday; has some form here too but she's not easy to recommend after that.

runners_data.name: Chicory
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won her Newbury maiden in good style but has been highly tried since and needs the pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Highly tried after winning debut; drops in grade for seasonal/handicap debut; could figure
runners_data.spotlight: All starts at 6f; won August Newbury maiden (good; form worked out) on her second start and highly tried in two subsequent runs, when down the field in Polytrack Group 3 and Newmarket Listed event; drops in grade for this seasonal/handicap debut and very interesting to see how she goes in the market.

races.paceDynamic: Barefoot Beach, Zighy, and Seven Fires will clash for the early lead, creating a genuine pace battle from the stalls. With three confirmed front-runners in a small field, the gallop will be strong and sustained throughout the 6f journey. Seven Fires brings the highest TopSpeed figure (71) and recent C&D form, while Barefoot Beach showed pace when winning at 25-1 last time. This pace setup will play directly into the hands of hold-up performers who can sit off the speed and finish strongly - the prominent runners and hold-up horses have a clear tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapses Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If all three front-runners go too hard early and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The sustained battle between Barefoot Beach, Zighy and Seven Fires will drain their stamina reserves, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past. Powdering and Chicory can exploit their superior closing kicks from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Seven Fires Dominates Gate
scenarios.trigger: If Seven Fires uses her class advantage to control the pace from the front
scenarios.body: Her superior TopSpeed rating of 71 and recent C&D success gives her the quality edge over the other leaders. She can dictate terms and kick clear when the others weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Fantasy Obsessor and Addarella get the perfect tracking position behind the speed
scenarios.body: The early pace battle allows the prominent runners to sit in the ideal stalking spot before launching their bids. Fantasy Obsessor's C&D win and Addarella's Wolverhampton form becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Barefoot Beach Repeats Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Barefoot Beach can again find improvement from her last winning run
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced 3yo could have more progression in her after that 25-1 Kempton success. Her front-running style might just be sustainable enough over this shorter trip.

watchPoints.text: Seven Fires could steal this if she breaks smartest and uses her class edge to avoid the early pace battle with the other two leaders
Watch for any market confidence behind Barefoot Beach or Zighy despite their front-running clash, as one might have tactical instructions to sit second
Powdering and Chicory both need the three leaders to go hard early - if the pace is steady, their closing kicks become less effective
Fantasy Obsessor and Addarella must get the perfect tracking positions to have any chance given their long absences and recent form concerns
The 8-runner field means less traffic problems but also fewer hiding places for the hold-up horses to get cover behind the pace
